title: `SUM` of integers returns `BIGINT`; 64-bit partial sums raise (ANSI) or wrap
verdict: `i8`…`i32` widen to `BIGINT`; `i64`: `ERROR` on a partial sum (ANSI), order-dependent; no values NULL
description: `sum` of `TINYINT`, `SMALLINT`, `INT` and `BIGINT` returns `BIGINT`, so the narrow widths cannot overflow (two `INT` maxima sum to 4294967294). A `BIGINT` sum adds in `BIGINT` with the `+` of the mode: under ANSI it raises `ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` as soon as a partial sum passes 64 bits, without ANSI it wraps. Whether a partial sum overflows depends on the order and the partitioning: 2⁶³ - 1, 1, -2 in one partition in that order raises, in the reverse order (or split over two partitions) it gives 2⁶³ - 2.
`sum` of no rows, or of NULLs only, is NULL; `count(x)` skips NULLs and is 0 there. `try_sum` gives NULL on overflow.
reference: `sum` of integers returns the input type, with `overflow: ERROR` on the true total (an inferred precondition checked on the data, #316, #437), and NULL for no values. Spark widens `i8`…`i32` (a cast back to the width raises where the reference does), and for `i64` raises on partial sums: `sverify.sql.spark` adds `DECIMAL(38,0)` values instead and checks the total.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
